solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Phone card used by single girl

parts.note: a SIM card sits inside a mobile phone
single means one

explanation.surface: A lone young woman pays for her calls with a prepaid card.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone is a woman's given name, so it fits the bare definition of a girl.

clue.text: Turbulent priest's mischievous essence

indicators.note: turbulent describes something stirred up and disordered, so the letters of the cleric are churned into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; only the word priest is the fodder

explanation.surface: A rowdy clergyman turns out to have an impish spirit about him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Henry II's 'turbulent priest'. The 's is a link meaning 'is', joining the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy, a small mischievous spirit, which the clue calls an essence.

clue.text: He takes in new worker to treat roughly

indicators.note: one word taking in others means it holds them inside itself, as a container

parts.note: he refers to a male person
a hand is a labourer or worker, as in farm hand

explanation.surface: A man hires a fresh labourer and then bullies him.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle someone is to push them about physically, handling them roughly.

clue.text: Attire close to sleeper

parts.note: nigh is an old word meaning near or close to
tie is the American word for a railway sleeper

explanation.surface: Clothing worn snug against someone asleep in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' suggests a person in bed, but it is the railway sleeper, called a tie in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, an item of clothing, so it is a kind of attire.

clue.text: Confined in the past by National military office

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in or confined
ago means at a time before now

explanation.surface: Someone long kept indoors by the national authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters building of the US Department of Defense, a military office.

clue.text: Lush country remedies all disorders

indicators.note: to disorder is to throw into confusion, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescriptions claim to cure every ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorders' reads as illnesses being cured, but it is a verb telling you to scramble REMEDIES and ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emerald Isle is a poetic name for Ireland, famous for its lush green countryside.

clue.text: Explorer set up company for product discovered in America

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed to North America for England

explanation.surface: A voyager founds a business to sell a crop found in the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns CABOT into TOBAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco was a New World plant that European explorers first encountered in the Americas.

clue.text: Such as Alfred, old king ruined tea

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: ruined means spoilt and broken up, so the letters of the drink are rearranged

explanation.surface: King Alfred famously spoiled something in the kitchen, here a pot of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Alfred burning the cakes. 'ruined' turns TEA into EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great is one of the few English kings given that title, so he is an example of a great king.

clue.text: Crazy man will make concise container

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy
the contraction he'll means he will, a man will

explanation.surface: A deranged fellow sets about building a compact box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' is a link. HE'LL drops its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutshell is literally the case holding a nut, and 'in a nutshell' means put concisely.

clue.text: Some degenerate turned to rat

indicators.note: turned means the run found is then read backwards
some of a word means only part of its letters are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A depraved person changes sides and becomes an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EGENER sit in 'degenerate'; 'turned' reverses them. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, and to rat on a deal means the same.

clue.text: Slightest charge favoured

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
blest, an old form of blessed, means favoured by fortune

explanation.surface: The smallest fee is the one most welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeblest means weakest, the least in strength, which the clue renders as slightest.

clue.text: Diner returned pie to spread around

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for the pastry is read in reverse

parts.note: a tart is a pastry pie

indicators.note: around means turned about, so this word is also read backwards

parts.note: to air an opinion is to spread it abroad

explanation.surface: A customer sends back a pie, and the complaint spreads round the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diner' suggests the eater, but it stands for the eatery; 'pie' is the TART reversed to begin, and spreading news is airing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant, the kind of place one dines; the clue uses a diner in the American sense of an eatery.

clue.text: Assemble natives o'er heart of America in their territory

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
to assemble is to put parts together into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Indigenous people gather above the centre of the American continent on their own land.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of AMERICA is R, its fourth of seven letters. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservation is land set aside for Native American peoples, their own territory.

clue.text: Nick is an attractive mate

definitions.meaning: to nick is to seize or arrest someone
a desirable partner is called a good find, someone worth landing

explanation.definitionFit: To catch a thief is to nick him, and a desirable partner is called a real catch.

clue.text: Looking stunning wearing armour perhaps made from soldered kilts

indicators.note: made from tells you the answer is formed out of these letters in another order

explanation.surface: A Highlander in welded kilts looks both glamorous and ready for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: dressed to kill is smartly dressed, and literally someone in armour is dressed for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed to kill means dressed very glamorously, and taken literally it describes armour for battle.

clue.text: One succeeds in getting sex appeal in great man right

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in here means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a hero is a great man
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An heir finds success by being attractive, inside a great man's circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. 'One succeeds' sounds like someone achieving success, but it means one who succeeds to an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritor is someone who succeeds another, taking their property or title.

clue.text: Sea food from El Salvador with endless fish served up

parts.note: ES is the international vehicle code for El Salvador

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are brought upwards, read in reverse
endless means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: pollack is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A Central American seafood platter of fish dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts POLLACK to POLLAC; 'served up' reverses it to CALLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An escallop is a scallop, a shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Part of London gives protection to former President

parts.note: to shepherd is to guard and guide, giving protection
George Bush, father and son, were both US Presidents

explanation.surface: A London district provides security for an ex-President.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's Bush is a district of west London.

clue.text: Cheer up to secure fruits of labour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rah is a cheer, as in hurrah
to vest is to secure a right or property firmly to someone

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for workers to lock in what they have earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAH into HAR. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered after a season's work, the reward of labour.

clue.text: Lie with girl following relative's tip-off

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the previous one
tip-off means the tip, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: an aunt is a relative; the possessive adds no letter
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A falsehood accompanies a woman who tipped off the police about her family.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a falsehood, a statement that is not true, much like a fib.

clue.text: Representing a star with luminance

indicators.note: read as re-presenting, presenting the letters again in a fresh order

parts.note: L is the standard symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: Something portraying a bright, glowing celestial body.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue defines a word meaning starry, while the anagram of A STAR plus L builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to or resembling the stars, and stars give off light.

clue.text: Criminal injury soldiers hate

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British criminal offence of injury
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops loathe the crime of assault.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is an offence in English law.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest or loathe it.

clue.text: Language from backward island

parts.note: hind means at the back or rear

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken on a remote, underdeveloped island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' wants to signal a reversal, but it is HIND, rear. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is one of the main official languages of India.

clue.text: A forward sure to mess up openings

parts.note: pert and forward both mean cheeky or bold

indicators.note: to mess up is to jumble, so the letters of this word are disordered

explanation.surface: A striker certain to fluff his chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a footballer but means PERT. 'to mess up' turns SURE into URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are openings or gaps.

clue.text: Stays mostly, that is ladies' underwear

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to linger is to stay on
IE abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Corsets, more or less, count as women's underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' suggests the old corset garment, apt for the definition, but it is the verb LINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Soft talk in club

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
to utter is to speak or talk

explanation.surface: Quiet conversation inside a social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'club' is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is a golf club used on the green.

clue.text: Australian batsman around start of innings making gesture

indicators.note: around means the batsman's name is wrapped about another letter

parts.note: Ricky Ponting was an Australian Test cricket captain and batsman

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An Aussie cricketer signals at the beginning of his innings.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a batsman's turn at the crease in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing means indicating with a finger, making a gesture.

clue.text: Church has spoken for singers

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: The church has given its word to the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music written for a choir, that is for singers.
